locator.section: 4 / Basic Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (charge migration, inductive cleavage 'i')

evidence.curator_note: Second, lower half of eq 4.38: the m/z 84 distonic hydrocarbon radical cation (carbenium at map 6, carbon radical at map 3) undergoes an inductive ('i') charge-site cleavage. The C4-C5 sigma bond ionizes heterolytically toward the cation: both electrons form the new C5=C6 double bond (releasing neutral ethylene, H2C=CH2, maps 5/6) and the positive charge migrates from map 6 to map 4, giving the m/z 56 ion (100%, base peak). The carbon radical on map 3 is a spectator throughout, so m/z 56 is again a distonic radical cation (butene radical cation). ARC COUNT: the book draws 1 arc -- a single full (double-barbed) arrow spanning the breaking C4-C5 bond into the forming C5=C6 bond; move <1> carries electron_count 2, so no implicit hook is required. 'Charge migration' (labelled on the page): the charge ends up on the hydrocarbon rather than on the lost neutral.

Cross-linked to MOD rule IMS_4_38_ind_2; VERIFIED against its DFS '[C]1[C]2[C.]3[C]4[C]5[C+]6 >> [C]1[C]2[C.]3[C+]4.[C]5{=}[C]6'. The rule breaks the C4-C5 bond, forms the C5=C6 double bond and moves the cation from map 6 to map 4 while the radical on map 3 is untouched -- exactly step_i_inductive_ethylene_loss (rule map numbers align 1:1 with this record). This is the standard charge-site inductive cleavage: the departing ethylene is the two carbons distal to the radical, and the charge relocates one carbon inward.
